title: Embedding Criterion: GF(pᵐ) ↪ GF(pⁿ) ⟺ m ∣ n
content: galoisField_embeds_iff_dvd is the heart of the entry: for m, n ≥ 1 there is an 𝔽ₚ-algebra homomorphism GF(p^m) →ₐ GF(p^n) iff m ∣ n. Because any field homomorphism is injective, 'the hom set is nonempty' already means GF(p^m) embeds as a subfield. The proof is three rewrites: FiniteField.nonempty_algHom_iff_finrank_dvd replaces 'Nonempty (K →ₐ L)' by 'finrank 𝔽ₚ K ∣ finrank 𝔽ₚ L', and two applications of GaloisField.finrank ([GF(p^k):𝔽ₚ] = k for k ≠ 0) turn the finrank-divisibility into the arithmetic statement m ∣ n. The mathematics — that an embedding is governed by divisibility of degrees — is Mathlib's; the contribution is the specialization to the canonical Galois fields in terms of their exponents.

title: Counting Embeddings and Endomorphisms
content: galoisField_natCard_algHom refines existence to a count: when m ∣ n there are exactly m distinct 𝔽ₚ-algebra embeddings GF(p^m) →ₐ GF(p^n), one for each conjugate of a primitive generator under Frobenius. It specializes FiniteField.natCard_algHom_of_finrank_dvd (= finrank 𝔽ₚ K) through GaloisField.finrank. The diagonal case m = n (galoisField_natCard_endo, via dvd_rfl) gives n endomorphisms of GF(p^n) — these are exactly the n powers of the Frobenius automorphism x ↦ x^p, i.e. the cyclic Galois group Gal(GF(p^n)/𝔽ₚ) ≅ ℤ/nℤ developed in the sibling Frobenius–Galois entries.

title: Subfield Degrees Are Exactly the Divisors of n
content: Two complementary theorems pin down the subfield structure. exists_subalgebra_finrank_of_dvd: for each divisor d ∣ n there is a subfield of GF(p^n) of degree exactly d — take an embedding GF(p^d) ↪ GF(p^n) (which exists by the criterion) and use AlgEquiv.ofInjectiveField to identify its image with GF(p^d), so the image has degree d (and cardinality p^d, exists_subalgebra_card_of_dvd). intermediateField_finrank_dvd: conversely the degree of ANY intermediate field 𝔽ₚ ⊆ K ⊆ GF(p^n) divides n, directly from the tower law [K:𝔽ₚ]·[GF(p^n):K] = [GF(p^n):𝔽ₚ] = n. Together: the set of subfield degrees of GF(p^n) is exactly the set of divisors of n. For GF(2^12) that set is {1,2,3,4,6,12}, the divisor lattice of 12. (Counting the distinct subfields — uniqueness of the subfield of each degree — is left as the follow-up open question.)

title: Concrete Instances
content: The criterion is made tangible: GF(2^2) embeds in GF(2^4) because 2 ∣ 4, but there is NO embedding GF(2^2) ↪ GF(2^3) because 2 ∤ 3 (proved by rewriting to ¬(2 ∣ 3) and decide). There are exactly 2 embeddings GF(2^2) →ₐ GF(2^4). And GF(2^12) has a degree-6 subfield (since 6 ∣ 12) but no degree-5 subfield (since 5 ∤ 12, via the divides-direction contrapositive). All divisibility side-conditions are discharged by norm_num / decide, keeping the examples axiom-free.
mathContext: $\mathrm{GF}(2^2) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{GF}(2^4)$, $\mathrm{GF}(2^2) \not\hookrightarrow \mathrm{GF}(2^3)$; $\mathrm{GF}(2^{12})$ has a degree-6 but no degree-5 subfield.
